```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(sonicscrewdriver)
```

## Managing labelled audio data in R with SonicScrewdriveR

### Setting annotation boundaries

SonicScrewdriveR provides a set of functionality to read, generate, manage and write label data for audio files. This `Annotation` class is used to consistently handle annotations to audio files. Annotations are delimited in the time domain (seconds) and frequency domain (Hz).

```{r}
a1 <- annotation(
  start = 0,
  end = 1
)

a2 <- annotation(
  low = 0,
  high = 1000
)
```

`Inf` can be used as a value to `end` or `high` to indicate that the annotation extends to the limits of the file.

```{r}
a3 <- annotation(
  start = 0,
  end = Inf
)

a4 <- annotation(
  low = 0,
  high = Inf
)
```

### Handling metadata

Objects of the `Annotation` class have inbuilt character slots for storing the file name (`file`) and the `source`, `type` and `value` of the annotation. A list slot `metadata` is provided for storing additional metadata.

Who made an annotation and when are held in the `identifiedBy` and `dateIdentified` slots, as Audiovisual Core gives them for a region of interest (`dwc:identifiedBy` and `dwc:dateIdentified`). `identifiedBy` is a person, or the software and model that made the annotation, while `source` is where the annotation came from. `dateIdentified` is ISO 8601 text, and a `Date` or a time given to `annotation()` is written as such, a time in UTC.

The `file`, `source`, `type`, `value` and `identifiedBy` slots are used by SonicScrewdriveR. For example, the `merge_annotations` function uses these slots to appropriately merge overlapping annotations, so that the annotations of two people are not merged into one unless asked.

When using tools from SonicScrewdriveR these slots may be pre-populated. The example below creates an `Annotation` object equivalent to one generated by the function `birdNetAnalyse`.

```{r}
a5 <- annotation(
  start=27,
  end=30,
  file = "example.wav",
  source = "BirdNet-Analyzer",
  type = "birdnet-detection",
  value = "sparrow",
  identifiedBy = "BirdNET-Analyzer 2.4",
  dateIdentified = as.POSIXct("2026-10-30 09:15:00", tz="UTC"),
  metadata = list(
    confidence = 0.9
  )
)
```

### Reading annotations

#### From audioblast database

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Fetch annotations from audioBlast as `Annotation` objects
a <- audioblast("data", "annomate", source="bio.acousti.ca", source_id=10754, output="Annotation")
```

#### From the cue points of a wave file

Audio editors save the markers and labelled regions someone has put on a recording as cue points in the wave file. `wavCues` reads them as `Annotation` objects: a labelled region runs from its position for its length, and a marker starts and ends where it is.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Read the markers and labelled regions saved in a wave file
a <- wavCues("marked.wav")
```

#### From an AOEF file

The Whombat annotation tool exports its projects in the Acoustic Objects Exchange Format (AOEF), the JSON format of the soundevent Python package. `readAOEF` reads them as `Annotation` objects, one for each tag of each sound event. The paths of the recordings in the file are relative to the directory the audio is in, which is given as `audio.dir`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Read the annotations of a project exported from Whombat
a <- readAOEF("project.json", audio.dir="audio")
```

### Generating annotations

#### Using BirdNET

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Analyse sound files using BirdNET-Analyzer
f <- system.file("extdata", "AUDIOMOTH.WAV", package="sonicscrewdriver")
annotations <- birdNetAnalyse(f, output="Annotation")
```

### Merging annotations

The `merge_annotations` function can be used to merge overlapping annotations. The function will merge annotations with overlapping time extents with the same `file`, `type`, `value` and optionally `source` and `identifiedBy` slots.

```{r}
a <- list(
  annotation(
    start=27,
    end=30,
    file = "example.wav",
    source = "BirdNet-Analyzer",
    type = "birdnet-detection",
    value = "sparrow",
    metadata = list(
      confidence = 0.9
    )
  ),
  annotation(
    start=30,
    end=33,
    file = "example.wav",
    source = "BirdNet-Analyzer",
    type = "birdnet-detection",
    value = "sparrow",
    metadata = list(
      confidence = 0.8
    )
  )
)

merge_annotations(a)
```

The two annotations in the list `a` overlap in time and have the same `file`, `type` and `value` slots. The `merge_annotations` function has merged these into a single annotation with the time extent from 27 to 33 seconds.

### Writing annotations

#### Audacity label file

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Convert the annotations to an Audacity label file
writeAudacityLabels(annotations, "birdnet_annotations.txt")
```

#### AOEF file

`writeAOEF` writes annotations to an AOEF file, which soundevent reads, and which Whombat imports as an annotation project. Annotations read by `readAOEF` are written back as they were read.

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Write the annotations as an annotation project
writeAOEF(annotations, "birdnet_annotations.json", audio.dir="audio", collection="annotation_project")
```
